title: the-verdict-vocabulary-is-held-by-postgres
owner: CC gates writes to cairn/devices/inference_domain/ and to cairn/devices/db_domain/ (both charters' gated_by). Nothing here stands at Akien's gate: the vocabulary is already stated in three places, and this only moves it from prose into the schema.
intention: The verdict column's vocabulary is held by Postgres rather than by prose: inference_calls.verdict admits 'miss', 'hit' and 'refused' and nothing else, refused at the database rather than trusted at three docstrings.
why: Law 4 in its plainest form. Since 2026-08-18 the column carries three values, and the three-value rule is written in cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py's column comment, in its module docstring, and in the charter — enforced in none of them. The lived symptom is not today's; it is the day a builder adds a fourth value. It lands silently in an append-only record of truth, and every reader that filters on verdict — _latest_valid_answer serving WHERE verdict='miss', yield_report summing hits and misses, three standing probes — starts answering a question nobody asked, with no surface saying so. A vocabulary enforced nowhere is an IOU, and this is the ticket the IOU asked for.
traces_to: Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy. Until it is, it is a tracked debt, not a resting state.
Law 7 — a record of truth may not carry an error quietly; a fourth verdict value written today would be counted as something it is not by every reader that filters on the column.
Law 6 — the constraint is declared through db_domain's one door (create_owned_table), never a hand psql.

falsifier.proves_green: Proof gate: cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_domain.py, run by the tester and sealed under netns — a tooth that creates an owned table carrying the constraint and asserts that an out-of-vocabulary write RAISES, plus a tooth over the standing table asserting the same once the child has applied it. Check-type: deterministic, and the deciding observation is a database refusal rather than a text match. Feedback-to-origin on failure: the WATCHME probe below deposits and pokes; re-opening is the owner's act (Law 6). Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed. Owner: CC (cairn/devices/inference_domain/intention+why.json, gated_by) for the column spec; the child's work lands in db_domain, whose charter gates separately.
falsifier.proves_red: FALSIFIER: DONE when an attempt to write a row whose verdict is outside the vocabulary is REFUSED BY POSTGRES on the STANDING table — proved by a tooth that tries the write and asserts the raise, never by reading the DDL. RED on any of: (1) the constraint is declared in _CACHE_COLUMNS but the standing table does not carry it, so production and a fresh install disagree about what is legal; (2) the vocabulary is enforced in Python at the writer instead — policy wearing physics' clothes, which is exactly what Law 4 names; (3) a tooth asserts DDL text or a pg_constraint row rather than the refusal of an actual write. HORIZON: the day a fourth verdict value is genuinely wanted. This should stop it loudly and be widened deliberately — a vocabulary that never refuses anything is a habit.

children: one child, and it proves first: a-standing-table-gains-its-constraint-through-the-one-door — db_domain gains the one thing it lacks, a way to bring an ALREADY-CREATED owned table up to the shape its column spec declares, through the one door rather than a hand psql. It is a child rather than a sibling because this cast cannot reach its own falsifier without it (the falsifier names the STANDING table), and it is a separate node rather than part of this one because it lands in a different device under a different charter's gate. It will be cast through its own /sorted firing. NAMING NOTE: the /sorted firing called it a-standing-table-reaches-its-declared-shape; the cast narrowed to a constraint primitive rather than a shape reconciler, and the id was corrected to match what will actually be built. The berth carries the older name.
how: Declare the CHECK in the column spec itself — "verdict": "text NOT NULL CHECK (verdict IN ('miss','hit','refused'))" in _CACHE_COLUMNS. create_owned_table passes each column's type through sql.SQL() raw (store.py:170-172), so a CHECK rides free with NO new db_domain primitive and no ALTER: a fresh install gets the physics at CREATE TABLE. What that does NOT reach is the STANDING table, already created without it — hence the child, which proves first.

watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: the distinct verdict values found past the era with a row count each, whether a check constraint over verdict exists on the live table, and its expression text if so.
watchme.consumer: the next builder to add a verdict value — who should meet a refusal rather than discover months later that a reader has been silently miscounting — and whoever next asks whether this system's vocabularies are enforced anywhere or merely written down.
watchme.enough: enough when, across reads spanning at least one build that touched the domain, the live table has carried the constraint on every read and every distinct verdict value found past the era has been inside the vocabulary. Both halves matter and they fail differently: an out-of-vocabulary value present means the constraint is absent or was dropped; the constraint present with only accounted values means the physics is doing its job silently, which is the passing state.
watchme.trigger: each read of inference_calls — the probe carries the distinct verdict values actually present past its era AND whether the LIVE table carries a check constraint over verdict, so it watches the declared shape and the running shape at the same moment. It rides existing traffic; no clock and no host.

standing_note: STANDING IN QUESTION AS OF 2026-08-18, UPDATED 2026-08-31. Original concern: the inference_calls table shape may change, making a three-value CHECK on verdict the wrong grain. UPDATE 2026-08-31 (Akien): the inference call becomes a TASK the inference proxy performs, producing an ARTIFACT of the process stored in .cairn (instance-space logging, not the DB table). The task ticket becomes the RETURN VALUE — the receiver or their shim extracts the actual reply, making the call inspectable. The three-value verdict vocabulary still needs enforcement but the mechanism changes: it examines a single artifact rather than constraining a DB column. Dependencies shift: state-machine-physics (BUILDME) is now upstream — task state transitions need the transition table enforced. The inference-call-comprehensive-task-ticket (TICKETME:waiting) must land first to settle the new shape. This ticket's falsifier, how, and gates will need recasting against the new shape once it lands.

decisions.text: The vocabulary is declared once, at ensure_cache: store.add_owned_constraint(CACHE, CACHE_OWNER, 'verdict_vocabulary', "verdict IN ('hit', 'miss', 'refused')") immediately after create_owned_table; _CACHE_COLUMNS keeps verdict as 'text NOT NULL' (no CHECK inside the column spec), so a fresh install and the standing table receive the constraint by the same act and cannot disagree — this supersedes the HOW's column-spec declaration because the child's door (db059208bbd9, PROVED 2026-08-26) exists now.

The child db059208bbd9 (store.add_owned_constraint) is already built and PROVED; the call in ensure_cache is idempotent and applies verdict_vocabulary to the standing inference_calls table on the first call after the build — no separate migration, no ALTER outside the one door, nothing to wait on.

Teeth live in cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_domain.py and are live write attempts, never DDL inspection alone: test_an_out_of_vocabulary_verdict_is_refused_at_the_database (a nonce table through create_owned_table + ensure_cache; a raw INSERT of verdict 'bogus' raises psycopg 23514 CheckViolation while 'hit', 'miss', 'refused' land), test_the_standing_table_refuses_an_out_of_vocabulary_write (one INSERT against the STANDING table, refused with 23514 and rolled back, the table left as found), and test_the_verdict_constraint_exists_on_the_table (an information_schema companion to the write teeth, never their substitute).

The probe berths at cairn/devices/inference_domain/probes/the_verdict_vocabulary_is_refused_at_the_database.py and declares a module-level frozen PROBE carrying both carry and enough per the ticket's watchme; test_the_probes_row_read_agrees_with_an_actual_write_refusal binds it at call time and holds its information_schema read against the refusal of an actual write.

Compose, do not rewrite: run python3 cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_domain.py whole (22 teeth) green twice locally, then the tester seals it under netns as the ticket's proven_by; the other inference_domain validations stand as they are — the constraint touches no reader and no other proof is edited.

The probe's shape is cairn.tools.base.probe.Probe (a frozen dataclass: why, trigger(now, context)->bool, to='inference_domain', body={'nexus':'hypothesize','kind':'efficacy'}, carry(context)->dict, enough(context)->bool, horizon=1000) — copy cairn/devices/librarian/probes/standing_moves_under_live_use.py's PROBE = Probe(...) block and replace its survey. test_the_probes_row_read_agrees_with_an_actual_write_refusal is a FOURTH tooth in test_inference_domain.py (beside D3's three, not inside the probe): it imports the probe module at call time via importlib, calls its survey_the_corpus(), and asserts constraint_exists is True exactly when the raw INSERT of an out-of-vocabulary verdict is refused with 23514.

22 is the count of test_ functions test_inference_domain.py holds AFTER the build (18 standing + the 4 of D3/D4); the chart's '17 (15+2)' was the 2026-09-02 plan and is superseded. The gate is the exit code: the file runs green twice (exit 0 both times); the tooth count is a diagnostic to report, never a pass condition.

D4 read with D6 and this line: the probe module is cairn/devices/inference_domain/probes/the_verdict_vocabulary_is_refused_at_the_database.py; its module-level PROBE is cairn.tools.base.probe.Probe, a frozen dataclass whose fields are exactly: why (str), trigger (callable (now, context) -> bool), to (str, here 'inference_domain'), verb (str, default ''), channel (str, default 'personal'), body (dict, here {'nexus': 'hypothesize', 'kind': 'efficacy'}), carry (callable (context) -> dict), while_true (bool, default False), enough (callable (context) -> bool), horizon (int, here 1000). The template to copy is the PROBE = Probe(...) block of cairn/devices/librarian/probes/standing_moves_under_live_use.py, both files readable in the repo; replace its survey with an information_schema.check_constraints read of the verdict_vocabulary clause on inference_calls. Nothing else in D4 is left to infer.
